root_cause_label: Agent failed to detect that commands produced no output from step 7 onward, entering a multi-cycle thrash loop of discovery-download-build attempts; even when downloads were eventually attempted, the agent used the wrong build target (generic Makefile search instead of unix.mak) and never produced the required binary
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent spent 131 steps cycling through the same broken discovery-download-build pattern without ever recognizing that commands were not executing or capturing output, and additionally lacked knowledge of POV-Ray 2.2's legacy unix.mak build system, resulting in no binary ever being produced.
t_err_evidence: At step 11, after step 7 returned '(command not found in terminal output)' for the Official-2.2 directory listing, the agent switches to heuristic brute-force guessing of archive filenames (povray-2.2.tar.gz, povray22.tar.gz, pov22src.tgz, etc.) rather than recognizing the output-capture problem. The filenames it guesses do not match the actual POV-Ray 2.2 archive naming convention (POVSRC.TAR.Z / POVSRC.ZIP). This is the earliest decisive wrong action.
t_commit_evidence: By step 26, the agent's brute-force probing loop has exhausted its filename list with no successes and begins a second iteration of the same pattern (re-parsing the directory, re-guessing names, conditionally downloading to generic filenames). From this point, given the agent's subsequent behavior of repeating the same broken cycle 3-4 more times and never correctly executing commands, the failing outcome is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 116 is the first step with an explicit observable failure signal: '-bash: /usr/local/bin/povray: No such file or directory' when the agent tries to run the sanity check, confirming that no binary was ever installed.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the false premise that its curl/download/build commands were executing successfully throughout steps 7-115, despite nearly all terminal outputs showing '(command not found in terminal output)'. Rather than recognizing this as a framework/execution problem, the agent continued issuing new commands as if prior steps had worked. Additionally, the agent had a knowledge gap about POV-Ray 2.2's build system: it repeatedly tried generic Makefile locations instead of 'make -f unix.mak' in the source directory, and was unaware that .TAR.Z archives require ncompress/uncompress.
forewarning_evidence: From step 7 onward, almost all commands produce '(command not found in terminal output)' rather than actual content. The agent's pattern of repeating curl fetches of the same Official-2.2 directory (steps 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 39, 40, 41, 54, 55, 56, 69...) without any useful output is a clear forewarning that commands are not executing properly. Despite this, the agent never acknowledges or investigates the output-capture failure.
